title: How Parkour Works
summary: Josh and Chuck explain parkour, the movement discipline born from the "natural method" of Georges Hébert, a French naval officer who saw Caribbean locals navigating obstacles during the 1902 Mount Pelée eruption on Martinique. Hébert's ideas inspired French military training; David Belle, son of a French Special Forces soldier, combined them with Bruce Lee's adaptability and created parkour in the Paris suburbs with his friend Sebastien Foucan, forming the Yamakasi group. They cover Luc Besson's films Yamakasi and Taxi 2, the 2002 BBC short Rush Hour, the late-1990s split that led to freerunning, the purist rules (always forward, use obstacles for efficiency), the Red Bull competitions and the World Freerunning and Parkour Federation, moves such as the cat leap, precision jump, speed wall and kong vault, the dangers of the sport, and advice on where to learn safely. The episode closes with listener mail choosing a winner in a gross-story contest from a fire service watch commander in Leeds, England.

segments.title: Opening banter and The Office reference
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck open with a joke about being asked to sit still, then discuss a parkour scene in season six of The Office and listeners who have requested an episode on parkour.

segments.title: Martinique 1902 and Georges Hebert's natural method
segments.summary: Hebert, a French naval officer, coordinated rescues during the 1902 Martinique volcanic eruption and watched locals move athletically around obstacles. This inspired his natural method of physical fitness and French military training, including obstacle courses.

segments.title: David Belle and the birth of parkour
segments.summary: Raymond Belle taught his son David the natural method. David, combining it with Bruce Lee's adaptability, created parkour in Lisses, a Paris suburb, with his friend Sebastien Foucan. They formed the Yamakasi group, and the name parkour came from the word with a k instead of a c.

segments.title: Media exposure: Luc Besson films and Casino Royale
segments.summary: Luc Besson's films Yamakasi and Taxi 2 in successive years brought parkour to mass media. Foucan appeared in the Casino Royale parkour chase opening. The sport spread to the public in the late nineties and early two thousands.

segments.title: Purists, freerunning split and the rules of parkour
segments.summary: Parkour purists follow rules of forward movement and using obstacles for efficiency. A rift in the late nineties split off freerunning after Foucan and Belle disagreed on whether backward movement is allowed. Freerunning also permits aesthetic moves. The World Freerunning and Parkour Federation motto is no obstacle, no freedom.

segments.title: BBC Rush Hour short and dangers of parkour
segments.summary: David Belle introduced parkour to Britain with the 2002 BBC short Rush Hour, which inspired imitators. Several accidents followed, including a 2009 death in Sacramento of a teen who fell from a parking deck. The hosts stress the sport is dangerous and requires high skill.

segments.title: Parkour and skateboarding comparison, corporate events
segments.summary: The hosts compare parkour with skateboarding, noting purists dislike the comparison and that skateboarding became commercialized through ads and corporate events. Parkour was also hired for corporate events.

segments.title: Competitions and Red Bull sponsorship
segments.summary: Once competition appeared, with Red Bull sponsoring the Art of Motion tournament and the Barclay World Freerunning Championships, purists objected to judged contests. MTV also airs Ultimate Parkour Challenge.

segments.title: Parkour moves: cat leap, precision jump, speed wall, kong vault
segments.summary: The hosts describe the cat leap for climbing onto a higher ledge, tuck and roll landings, the kong vault with its animal-like hand push and leg pass, the precision jump, and the speed wall vault.

segments.title: Learning parkour safely
segments.summary: The hosts advise finding local groups or jams through parkour.com, noting academies, indoor facilities and YouTube channels as resources, and recommending helmets, knee pads and caution, especially for beginners.

segments.title: Banter about learning a kong leap
segments.summary: Chuck and Josh joke about Josh secretly learning a kong leap to surprise Chuck in New York.

segments.title: Gross-story contest: Matt from Leeds
segments.summary: Matt, a fire service watch commander in Leeds, England, wins a gross-story contest against his wife, an A and E nurse, with a story of nine inches of a patient's intestines draped over his leg. Hosts pick this over a fish-tail-in-rectum story. They also invite listeners to send stories of valuable finds.
